abstract:
We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models [Peters et al. (2018a)](#bib.bib36 ""); [Radford et al. (2018)](#bib.bib38 ""), BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference, without substantial task-specific architecture modifications.
BERT is conceptually simple and empirically powerful. It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).

bibliographic.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (NAACL-HLT 2019)

content.problem: Pre-trained language representations relied on unidirectional language models, and this unidirectionality restricted pre-training architectures and harmed downstream tasks that need context from both directions.
content.proposed_solution: The authors pre-train a bidirectional Transformer using masked language modeling and next sentence prediction objectives, then fine-tune all parameters with one task-specific output layer.
dataset_testbed: GLUE benchmark (MNLI, QQP, QNLI, SST-2, CoLA, STS-B, MRPC, RTE, WNLI)

metrics.name: GLUE score
metrics.condition: Official GLUE leaderboard score for BERT_LARGE, which includes WNLI. The paper's Table 1 average excludes WNLI and is 82.1.

metrics.name: average accuracy
metrics.condition: BERT_BASE average across GLUE test tasks in Table 1, which excludes WNLI.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.condition: BERT_LARGE on the GLUE MultiNLI matched test set in Table 1.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: Ensemble of 7 BERT_LARGE systems fine-tuned on TriviaQA and then SQuAD v1.1, test set.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: Single BERT_LARGE system with TriviaQA augmentation on the SQuAD v1.1 test set.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: BERT_LARGE on the SQuAD v2.0 test set.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.condition: BERT_LARGE on the SWAG test set.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: BERT_LARGE fine-tuned on CoNLL-2003 named entity recognition, test set averaged over 5 random restarts.

content.claim: Pre-training a deep bidirectional Transformer with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction achieved new state-of-the-art results on eleven NLP tasks and outperformed task-specific architectures after simple fine-tuning.

evidence.problem_quote: We argue that current techniques restrict the power of the pre-trained representations, especially for the fine-tuning approaches. The major limitation is that standard language models are unidirectional, and this limits the choice of architectures that can be used during pre-training.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: In this paper, we improve the fine-tuning based approaches by proposing BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT alleviates the previously mentioned unidirectionality constraint by using a “masked language model” (MLM) pre-training objective, inspired by the Cloze task [Taylor (1953)](#bib.bib43 "").
evidence.claim_quote: It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).
